findings.title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential is not found or belongs to another user, the handler throws a generic Error. tRPC turns this into a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR rather than a NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN response, so clients cannot tell an access denial from a server failure. It should throw a TRPCError with an appropriate code.

findings.title: connectedCalendars query not invalidated after cache deletion
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation, it never invalidates utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. As a result the UI keeps showing the stale 'Last updated' status and the 'Delete cached data' option even after the cache rows have been removed.

findings.title: Date formatting hardcoded to en-US
findings.body: The cache timestamp is formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US') while the surrounding label is localized. Non-US users will see a US-style date and time regardless of their locale. It should use the user's locale or the app's date formatting helpers.

findings.title: updateMany with empty data likely doesn't bump updatedAt
findings.body: updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object. Prisma may skip the update or not apply @updatedAt when no fields are set, so the timestamp may never change. This also adds an extra database write to every cache fill for a value the PR description says the frontend does not use.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired rows and runs even when caching is disabled
findings.body: The groupBy query does not filter on expiresAt, so a credential whose cache has fully expired is still reported as having a cache. The connectedCalendars handler also always uses the real CalendarCacheRepository rather than the feature-flagged mock, so this extra query runs for every user, including those without the calendar-cache feature.

findings.title: `sed -i ''` only works on macOS
findings.body: The script uses BSD sed syntax (`sed -i ''`), which fails on GNU/Linux sed, so updating GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in the env file breaks there. Separately, ENV_FILE is set to a path relative to the current working directory ('../.env'), so running the script from anywhere other than the expected directory edits or creates the wrong file.
